Not inherited, matching CSS, since decoration PROPAGATION is not modelled — set it on the text item itself. Defaults to `none`.

textOrientation.description: Mirrors CSS `text-orientation`, as a subset, and is consulted only inside a vertical block. Inherited; defaults to `mixed`.

textOverflow.description: What text does when it exceeds a DEFINITE box height; an auto-height box grows instead and never consults this. On a vertical block the overflow axis is the box width. Not inherited; defaults to `visible`.

textSpacingTrim.description: Mirrors CSS `text-spacing-trim`, as a subset. Trims the internal space between adjacent fullwidth punctuation glyphs to half-width. Synthesized after shaping, so it works on every face rather than depending on font features. Inherited; defaults to `space_all`, which trims nothing.

verticalAlign.description: Vertical alignment of content within the item's own box, which needs a definite height or `minHeight` slack to have room to act. On a vertical block it maps CSS-logically onto the column stack — top is the right edge, bottom the left. Not inherited; defaults to `top`.

writingMode.description: Mirrors CSS `writing-mode`, as a two-value subset. `vertical_rl` turns a text item into a vertical block — characters fill top to bottom and columns lay out right to left. Honoured on every text surface; a text `mark:` is the one warned fallback, `vertical_text_unsupported`. Inherited; defaults to `horizontal_tb`.

TableHeaderSpec.description: The header row's height and styling. It is chrome rather than a bound element, so `row.conditionalStyles` never reaches it.

height.description: A fixed height for the header row.

style.description: The header row's style layer. Its `backgroundColor` replaces the default header fill.

styleNames.description: Named `styles:` entries layered under the header's inline style, in listed order.

visuallyHidden.description: Whether the header row paints nothing — no label glyphs, no band fill, no grid ruling — while the labels stay in the PDF's text layer, so an extractor, a search index or an AI can still tell what each column means. Defaults to false. The row KEEPS its height, and a `headerGroups` row is hidden with it. Not a structure tree: no tagged PDF is emitted, so a screen reader gets the labels as flowing text with no header-to-column association. The table's own outer frame is not the row's and still draws across the strip.

Template.description: One document's template file: page geometry, the optional named-style and format registries, the presentation defaults, and the sections whose items produce content. Every wire struct rejects unknown keys, so a typo is a located parse error rather than a silent "unset", and non-finite numbers are refused anywhere in the document.

defaults.description: The document's presentation defaults: the style cascade root, which the `rem` unit also follows, and the per-type format defaults.

document.description: Metadata written into the PDF's `/Info` dictionary and XMP. PDF only: PNG previews carry no metadata.

formats.description: The named format registry a binding's `format:` may reference — date and datetime patterns given a name once and reused. At most 256 entries.

name.description: The template's own name. Informational — the engine never renders it.

page.description: Page size, orientation and margin. Omitted means A4 portrait with a 25 pt margin.

styles.description: The named-style registry items reference through `styleNames`, the CSS-class analogue. At most 256 entries (`too_many_styles`); styles are flat, so one cannot reference another.

version.description: An author-owned version marker. The engine records it and interprets nothing; a number or a string both parse and round-trip in the form they were written.

TemplateDefaults.description: Document-wide presentation defaults, the CSS `:root` analogue. A placement binds its key; how a date or an amount LOOKS is decided once here, so changing a default changes every placement that did not override it. Every key is omitted when unset, so an untouched template writes back without this block.

currency.description: The document's currency CODE, as ISO 4217. The middle of the currency fallback chain — a field's own `currency:`, then this, then the pack's default, then `JPY` — which is what lets a currency binding stay a bare key with no per-field code.

formats.description: Per-type format defaults, one per engine field type. Unknown type keys are parse errors.

locale.description: The document's locale id, as a BCP 47 tag. It selects the locale pack, which drives dates, currency display, grouping separators and units. On the CLI it is the fallback when `--lang` is absent.

style.description: The cascade ROOT style. Inherited properties flow from here into every item, and the `rem` unit resolves against this style's computed font size, falling back to the engine's 10 pt when unset.

TextAlign.description: Inline alignment within the line box. `left` and `right` name the block's start and end edges, and `center` splits the remaining space; on a vertical block those edges are the column's top and bottom.

TextCombineUpright.description: Tate-chu-yoko: `none` combines nothing, `all` combines the whole styled scope into one upright cell, and the map form `{ digits: n }` combines runs of up to n consecutive ASCII digits, with n from 2 to 4.

TextDecoration.description: A decoration line drawn on text. `none` draws nothing; `underline` draws below the baseline; `line_through` draws across the glyphs. On a vertical block an underline becomes the side line right of the em cell, following the JLREQ convention.

TextMark.description: The oval overlaid on a text item's glyph band. Its presence may be params-driven while its geometry stays derived from the glyphs, so an unmatched mark changes nothing about the layout.

data.description: The presence binding. Absent means always draw, which is the pure-decoration case; with `equals` or as a boolean it draws only on a match.

padding.description: The clearance between the glyph band and the oval. Unset applies an em-proportional default with a perceptual OVERSHOOT baked in, since a round shape flush with the caps reads smaller than it is. A negative value clamps so the oval stays positive.

style.description: The oval's decoration subset — border width and colour, background colour and opacity — with a 1 pt outline default when no layer authors a width.

styleNames.description: Named `styles:` entries layered under the mark's inline style, in listed order.

TextOrientation.description: How characters sit inside a vertical column. `mixed` keeps CJK and kana upright and rotates Latin and digits 90 degrees clockwise; `upright` keeps every character upright.

TextOverflow.description: What text does when it exceeds a definite box height. `visible` overflows and reports it; `shrink` reduces the computed font size until the content fits; `ellipsis` truncates and appends an ellipsis; `clip` cuts at the box edge with no marker.

TextSpacingTrim.description: How the internal space around fullwidth punctuation is trimmed. `space_all` trims nothing, leaving output unchanged; `normal` trims the space between two adjacent fullwidth punctuation glyphs to half-width; `trim_start` also trims a fullwidth opening bracket sitting at a line head.

TrackSpec.description: A grid axis: a COUNT, which splits the content size equally after the gaps, or a LIST of tracks mixing lengths, `fr` weights and `auto`.

Version.description: An author-owned version marker: a number or a string, kept in the form it was written so the file round-trips. The engine does not interpret it.

VerticalAlign.description: Block-axis alignment of content within the item's box. `top`, `middle` and `bottom` name the box's start, centre and end; on a vertical block they map CSS-logically onto the column stack, so `top` is the right edge.

VisibleBinding.description: The predicate deciding whether an item is shown, available on every item. It is the form-mark presence binding generalized to the whole item vocabulary — the same keys, the same truth table, the same diagnostics about a literal that can never match — plus a choice about the SPACE the item leaves behind. A key missing from params, or one that simply does not match, hides the item SILENTLY, so a blank form draws nothing and says nothing.

collapse.description: Whether a hidden item is removed from layout entirely rather than reserving its box. Defaults to false, the form-mark posture, where everything around the item stays exactly where it was so a blank-versus-filled params pair never shifts the layout by a point. True closes the siblings up over it and takes the separating gap with it.

equals.description: The value the field must equal for the item to show. Equality is TYPE-STRICT, so the string `"2"` never matches the number 2, and an array value is a multi-select — the item shows when the array CONTAINS this value, which is what a checkbox group's params look like. Omitted, the value is read as a boolean and the item shows when it is true.

key.description: The params field to read, as a dotted path. Required.

scope.description: Which data the key resolves against inside a repeat cell. Defaults to `element`, so each element decides for itself; `document` is the escape a page-global flag needs.

WritingMode.description: The block and inline directions of a text surface. `horizontal_tb` is the default — lines run left to right and stack downward. `vertical_rl` turns a text item into a vertical block: characters fill top to bottom and columns lay out right to left.

description: Per-key facts of the Shojiku template and definitions wire, derived from the parser. Regenerate with `make reference:generate`; `make reference:check` fails on drift.
